transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because something happened at work. I pushed ahead with an onboarding launch and committed company money and vendor time before the approvals were actually in place. At the time it felt bold, like it was necessary and I was just getting things done, but now I’m on leave and everyone’s asking what I was thinking.
Before you made that decision at work, did you feel unusually energized, like you didn’t need much sleep, or that your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

Yes, I felt like I had to keep moving. I was getting in early, walking around the floors, rewriting presentations, sending emails, shifting plans around. It was like my body had a motor in it, honestly. Sitting at my desk felt almost impossible.
Did you find yourself needing less sleep than usual during that time?
I’m not really sure. I know I was staying busy and up later than usual some nights, but I can’t say clearly that I needed less sleep. I wasn’t paying close attention to it at the time.
During that time, did you feel unusually confident or high-spirited, like you could take on more than usual or that things were going really well?

Yes. For the past few weeks I felt kind of brilliantly alive, like I could finally show leadership what HR could be if someone really pushed it. I felt more confident than usual, definitely.

But it wasn’t just upbeat. If someone questioned me, even about a small edit or a routine budget question, I could get suddenly furious. It felt like they were slowing down something obvious.

Can you describe how long this feeling of being 'brilliantly alive' and more confident than usual lasted? Was it a distinct period that built up and then let up, or did it stay more or less the same over time?

It’s been building for about a month, I’d say. It started around when the new executive began pushing back on my onboarding redesign. At first it was just me trying to respond to that, but then the confidence and intensity kept ramping up. It hasn’t really felt like my normal baseline.
Did you notice your mood being consistently elevated, expansive, or unusually irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, during this period?

Yes, most days it was there. Either I felt really energized and confident, like I could finally prove what HR should be doing, or I’d get irritable fast if someone pushed back. Even small things, like edits or budget questions, could make me suddenly furious. It wasn’t just a passing mood for an hour or two.
During this time when you felt so energized and confident, did it last continuously for at least a full week, without significant breaks, where you felt this way most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, it did. It’s been pretty continuous for weeks now—really building over about a month, since that new executive started challenging my onboarding redesign. I don’t think there were any real breaks where I felt back to normal for more than a short time.
